lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: the conditional probability formula as a fraction of outcomes
lessonRef.title: Reteach and varied practice: the conditional probability formula as a fraction of outcomes

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: These two examples show the same idea in two different formats.

items.prompt: P(delay | rain) = P(delay). What does that mean?
10 items, 4 defective, draw 2 without replacement. Both defective?

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: Given P(A and B) = 11/20 and P(B) = 12/20, find P(A | B) as a fraction in lowest terms.
Given P(A) = 3/20, P(B) = 6/20, and P(A and B) = 2/20, find P(A or B) in lowest terms.
In a study, the probability of a delay is the same whether or not it is raining. What is the correct interpretation?
choices: Delay and rain are independent, because conditioning on rain does not change the probability of a delay.
The two conditional probabilities are equal, so the order of conditioning never matters.
The two events are mutually exclusive.
The relationship proves that one event causes the other.

items.prompt: A box holds 7 items, of which 4 are defective. Two are drawn without replacement. Find the probability that both are defective, in lowest terms.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Given P(A and B) = 3/20 and P(B) = 4/20, find P(A | B) as a fraction in lowest terms.
Given P(A) = 5/20, P(B) = 7/20, and P(A and B) = 4/20, find P(A or B) in lowest terms.
In a study, P(has the condition | tested positive) is much smaller than P(tested positive | has the condition). What is the correct interpretation?
choices: The two events are mutually exclusive.
The relationship proves that one event causes the other.
The two conditional probabilities are equal, so the order of conditioning never matters.
The two conditional probabilities condition on different events, so they need not be close; a rare condition makes the first much smaller.

items.prompt: A box holds 9 items, of which 3 are defective. Two are drawn without replacement. Find the probability that both are defective, in lowest terms.
Given P(A and B) = 19/100 and P(B) = 50/100, find P(A | B) as a fraction in lowest terms.
